A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural Graph Pattern Machine research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite the expanded title and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original node classification, link prediction, graph classification/regression, OOD, scalability, and ablation results, including additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in its main text and appendices. Retention from v1 does not change their status as original results.

M1.justification: The random-walk tokenizer, semantic and anonymous path encoders, transformer pattern identifier, multi-scale learning, and test-time augmentation remain unchanged. Revised scaling configurations and newly disclosed dataset-specific choices do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same predictive datasets, ACM/DBLP and Twitch distribution shifts, CSL/EXP/SR25 expressiveness benchmarks, and TreeNeighborsMatching scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark, OOD, expressiveness, and scalability comparisons retain the same comparator membership. The additional related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported GPM scaling architectures change substantially within one retained analysis: hidden dimensions change from 512/1536/2048/3072/7168 to 64/256/256/512/1024, alongside revised layers and heads (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 7). Splits and metrics remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The component, encoder, multi-scale, test-time augmentation, expressiveness, over-squashing, sampling-bias, and interpretation analyses are retained. The sampling-bias discussion and plot promoted into the main text already appeared in v1 Appendix H.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 in both versions states five runs with different random seeds. The uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged, with no added confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run procedures.

E6.justification: All matched performance and timing tables retain identical entries, and the plots retain their results. For example, GPM's Products accuracy remains 82.62±0.39 and ZINC error remains 0.064±0.004. The new hyperparameter table documents settings rather than additional outcomes.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.4 explicitly states the reconstruction-conjecture condition already present in v1's appendix. Appendix C.3 revises the long-walk segmentation argument to acknowledge approximate aggregation rather than full reconstruction. The remaining proofs and complexity derivation are substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: direct graph-pattern learning, applicability across graph tasks, greater expressiveness, and favorable robustness, scalability, and interpretability. The expanded title and rewritten wording do not establish a new core contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly acknowledges that anonymous sub-walks lose node identity across segments and cannot fully reconstruct a long walk. Section 4.4 also describes test-time augmentation as having a negligible performance drop rather than no sacrifice. Most conclusion limitations are relocated from v1 Appendix E.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data repository link and Table 6 specifying selected learning rates, dropout, weight decay, batch sizes, positional encodings, anonymous-path encoders, and weights across all 18 predictive datasets. This substantially expands v1's defaults and search ranges into dataset-specific reproducibility information. Scaling architecture documentation is also revised.

R1.justification: v2 adds random-walk/path literature, including Chen et al. (2025), Michel et al. (2023), and Graziani et al. (2024), plus application and future-work citations. It removes the graph-to-text work by Wang et al. (2024). The principal positioning against message passing remains intact.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and opening introduction are revised; related work gains topical subdivisions; limitations move into the conclusion; and the existing sampling analysis receives a main-text summary. Most method, experiment, and appendix prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the hyperparameter table and moves v1 Figure 7's sampling-bias plots into the main text as Figure 5. Existing displays are resized or repositioned with consequent renumbering and page reflow; the underlying diagrams and result graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The dataset-specific configurations, code/data link, revised scaling documentation, and explicit theoretical qualifications improve reproducibility and transparency. These gains are limited by remaining inconsistencies: Table 6 includes PE dimension 16 outside the stated search range of 4, 8, and 20, and acknowledging approximate walk segmentation does not complete the expressiveness proof.
